.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 238 PM EDT Monday...

1. Periods of showers tonight into tomorrow. 

2. Heavier and more widespread rain Wednesday night with some 
embedded thunderstorms. 

3. Showery weather Friday trending drier by early next week as 
upper low pressure departs to the east. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 238 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The surface high that brought the lower humidity and 
sunshine today will gradually retreat to the east going into the day 
tomorrow, as a low will attempt to push a warm front through. 
However, it will fail to fully gain entry into the region and a 
stationary boundary will end up getting stationed over or just south 
of the region into Wednesday. 

An area of steady rain will push into the region late tonight and 
tomorrow morning, but most areas should just see an area of 
relatively light stratiform precipitation and only pick up a couple 
tenths of an inch, with the Northeast Kingdom possibly remaining 
completely dry. However, an area of elevated convection may just 
clip southern Vermont and St. Lawrence County and could lead to 
locally higher totals of 1-1.5 inches. A few rumbles of thunder are 
possible in those areas as well. However, it should occur over 
several hours and the threat for flash flooding is very low. The 
best synoptic forcing exits in the morning and despite the boundary 
remaining around, there should only be a couple scattered showers 
going through the day, but it will likely be dreary.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A more dynamic low pushes through Wednesday night into 
Thursday morning, bringing rounds of heavy rain. This one currently 
looks to make it just far enough northeast that the center passes 
through. Therefore, the associated elevated convection looks to be 
able to enter the region and bring periods of heavy rain and 
embedded thunderstorms. However, due to the temperature profiles and 
the nighttime occurrence, everything should remain elevated and not 
be severe. It will be continued to be watched if the dynamics from 
the storm would be strong enough to cause a couple storms with hail 
or gusty winds to break the inversion at the surface. Currently, 
most areas should receive around an inch of rain, but convective 
enhancement will cause locally higher totals. GEFS/EPS/CMCE 
probabilities of receiving more than an inch range between 25-50 
percent and the probabilities of 2 inches are below 10 percent, but 
the convective enhancement is not taken into account in those. The 
flood threat is low at this point. The one thing that will continued 
to be watched if the axis of heavy convective rain lines up with the 
axis tonight, but even then there will be multiple days in between 
and marginal totals.

KEY MESSAGE 3: An upper low will swing across eastern Maine 
Friday/Friday night, bringing yet another round of showers, 
especially over the northern high terrain. This feature will not 
make much eastward progress over the weekend, keeping us under 
cyclonic flow. There may be just enough moisture wrapping back into 
the region to keep the threat of showers around, especially in the 
afternoons, but don't anticipate a washout by any means. 
Temperatures may be a little on the cooler side, especially on the 
higher summits, but this will depend on how much eastward progress 
the upper low is able to make. Have stayed with the NBM/WPC forecast 
for now since we're a ways out, but adjustments may need to be made 
as the weekend draws closer.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 18Z Tuesday...VFR conditions to prevail at all terminals
through at least the first half of the TAF period. Clouds will
increase and lower overnight as a frontal boundary sets up over or
just to the SW of the region. Rounds of showers will ride along this
boundary tonight into Tuesday. Ceilings dropping to MVFR after 08z
at SLK/RUT and perhaps MSS, with visibility 5-6SM in rain showers
through the remainder of the period. Another round of valley fog is
possible late tonight into early Tuesday as well, mainly at EFK/MPV
where clouds will be slowest to arrive. While not as extensive as
this morning, anticipate at least periods of IFR/LIFR at these two
terminals 08z-13z, with visibility restrictions most likely at EFK.
MPV is more uncertain, with equal chances of IFR due to visibility
or ceilings. Winds will remain light and variable through the TAF
period, generally 5 kt or less.

Outlook...

Tuesday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Definite SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Definite
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.

Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
